ai.description: *Cnemaspis gracilis* reaches 40 mm SVL. It is grey-brown with a pale vertebral stripe and dark lateral spots. Distinctive features include a slender body, keeled ventral scales, and a tail lacking whorls.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Cnemaspis gracilis* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, continuous series of enlarged, keeled tubercles forming a clear dorsolateral row along its flanks.
ai.habitat: *Cnemaspis gracilis* inhabits rocky outcrops and boulders within dry deciduous forests and scrublands, typically found at low to moderate elevations in the Indian Peninsula.
ai.behavior: The Graceful Day Gecko is primarily nocturnal, emerging at night to hunt small insects on rock surfaces and tree trunks within its tropical habitat.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Cnemaspis gracilis* is oviparous, laying a clutch of two spherical, hard-shelled eggs. Breeding occurs throughout the year, peaking during the monsoon and post-monsoon.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Cnemaspis gracilis* is endemic to the southern Western Ghats in Tamil Nadu and Kerala, typically inhabiting rocky areas at elevations between 200 and 1,000 meters.
